title: UN Report: Gang Violence Has Shuttered Haiti's Newsrooms; 14 Journalists Killed Since 2021
detail: A United Nations News investigation published in May 2026 documented the systematic destruction of Haiti's media landscape by gang violence and insecurity over five years of crisis since the Moïse assassination. According to data compiled by UNESCO and UN BINUH, 14 media workers have been killed since 2021, creating a climate of fear that has forced journalists to self-censor, relocate, or flee the country entirely. Major outlets have been displaced or shuttered: Le Nouvelliste, Haiti's oldest newspaper founded in 1898, lost its historic downtown Port-au-Prince headquarters in February 2024 when gang forces expanded to occupy surrounding streets; Radio Magik 9 abandoned its premises under direct gang threats; and numerous smaller community radio stations — which serve as the primary information source for Haitians in rural and gang-controlled areas — have ceased broadcasting after gang attacks on their facilities. Journalists attempting to report from gang-controlled neighborhoods, which comprise over 80% of Port-au-Prince's metropolitan area, face constant threats from criminal groups as well as harassment from Haitian security forces that sometimes target journalists documenting their operations. A documented brain drain has seen significant numbers of Haitian journalists flee to Canada, France, and the United States, stripping the country of experienced reporters during a period of maximum public information need. The UN report notes that the systematic erosion of Haiti's independent press compounds the governance and accountability crisis, prevents civilian access to information about security conditions and humanitarian assistance, and allows gang narratives to circulate unchallenged in many communities. UNESCO and international journalist protection organizations called for dedicated protection protocols for Haitian journalists and digital security support for exiled media outlets continuing to cover Haiti from abroad.

media.caption: UN report: gang violence has killed 14 Haitian journalists since 2021, shuttered historic newsrooms including Le Nouvelliste, and driven a journalist brain drain
